_comment: Lifecycle behaviour test matrix. Each scenario is exercised by src/testing/lifecycleRunner.ts, which runs a full day-by-day oracle diff against the simulator. Rules referenced here are defined in the coverage ledger (docs/lifecycle-coverage-ledger.md).

scenarios.name: DAS retention count boundary
scenarios.description: Inactive chain must NOT be deleted on day (retentionCount-1) and MUST be deleted on day retentionCount when SLA also expired. Validates AND logic for count+SLA.

scenarios.name: DAS SLA prevents deletion when count expired but SLA not expired
scenarios.description: Chain has > retentionCount total points (count-expired) but the newest point in the sealed chain is still within slaDays. Chain must be preserved.

scenarios.name: DAS GFS preserves chain past standard retention
scenarios.description: A chain whose newest point is a weekly GFS full must NOT be deleted when standard retention+SLA have both expired; it must survive for the full GFS window (2 weeks = 14 days from tagging).

scenarios.name: GFS expiry order: oldest weekly removed first
scenarios.description: With weekly=2, when a 3rd weekly tag is applied the oldest (W3→W1 shift) must be untagged first. No point with weekly flag must exist beyond its retention window.

scenarios.name: Monthly GFS lands only on last Saturday of month
scenarios.description: A monthly GFS tag must appear on the last Saturday of each calendar month and not on any other Saturday.

scenarios.name: Yearly GFS lands only on last Saturday of December
scenarios.description: A yearly GFS tag must appear exactly on the last Saturday of December and never on any other Saturday.

scenarios.name: GFS tags stack on same Saturday restore point
scenarios.description: When weekly + monthly conditions are both true for the same Saturday, the single SyntheticFull must have both isWeeklyGFS and isMonthlyGFS set (no separate point created).

scenarios.name: SOBR Move: offload fires on exact offloadAfterDays boundary
scenarios.description: Chain sealed at day D. Points must still be in Performance on day D+offloadAfterDays-1 and must be in Capacity on day D+offloadAfterDays.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move: archive fires on exact capTierAge >= archiveAfterDays boundary
scenarios.description: After chain offloads to Capacity, a GFS-tagged point must NOT enter Archive until capTierAgeDays >= archiveAfterDays.

scenarios.name: SOBR Copy: archive fires only after pointAge >= offloadAfterDays + archiveAfterDays
scenarios.description: In copy mode the archive gate is total point age, not cap-tier age. Point must not appear in Archive before age = offloadAfterDays + archiveAfterDays.

scenarios.name: SOBR Copy: non-GFS Capacity residue pruned when GFS full archives
scenarios.description: When a GFS SyntheticFull in a chain archives (copy mode), non-GFS points in that chain must be pruned from Capacity. Performance copy must still remain accessible.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move: Performance pruning cannot precede offload completion
scenarios.description: On the day of offload completion chain.performancePrunedAt must still be null. Prune must not happen until offloadComplete=true AND retention/SLA expired AND GEN immutability cleared.

scenarios.name: DAS 3-year soak: W+M+Y GFS invariants every day
scenarios.description: Over 3 years, daily assertions: weekly count ≤ limit, monthly count ≤ limit, yearly count ≤ limit, GFS tags only on SyntheticFull/Full, exactly one global base per job.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move-only 3-year soak: tier ordering invariants every day
scenarios.description: No point may be in Archive without passing through Capacity. Prune before offload is forbidden. Active chains must never be offloadComplete.

scenarios.name: SOBR Copy-only 3-year soak: capacity residue and archive gate every day
scenarios.description: Scan every day: after any archive event for a chain the non-GFS Capacity residue must immediately be zero. Archive gate must never be violated.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move W+M+Y 5-year soak: full model over extended horizon
scenarios.description: 5-year soak exercising the full policy stack: daily GFS count limits, tier ordering, prune sequencing, chain deletion gating, SLA minimum, and base identity.

scenarios.name: DAS 5-year soak: SLA minimum guarantee never violated
scenarios.description: Over 5 years verify that no chain point dated within slaDays of current date is ever deleted, regardless of count-based expiry pressure.

scenarios.name: DAS 3-year drift: inactive chains and RP count never accumulate
scenarios.description: Over 3 years, assert every day that inactive chains never exceed 3 (steady-state max) and total restore points never exceed 42 (2×retention + GFS limits + buffer). Catches chain cleanup failures and pruning regressions that only manifest over long horizons.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move 3-year drift: inactive chains and RP count never accumulate
scenarios.description: Over 3 years with SOBR Move mode, assert that inactive chains never exceed 4 (offload + immutability extend chain lifetime but should still plateau) and total restore points never exceed 78 (2×retention=30 + GFS limits + buffer). Detects SOBR-specific chain lifecycle failures over extended runs.

scenarios.name: DAS high-retention 3-year drift: retention=30 with full GFS never accumulates
scenarios.description: Higher retention (30 days) with full W+M+Y GFS over 3 years. Max inactive chains ≤ 3, max restore points ≤ 75 (2×30 + 9 + buffer). Validates that the engine scales correctly with larger retention windows without drift.

scenarios.name: Performance immutability blocks Performance prune
scenarios.description: Chain is retention+SLA expired and offloadComplete, but performanceImmutabilityDays has not elapsed since GEN window end. Prune must not fire until the lock expires.

scenarios.name: Capacity immutability blocks chain deletion
scenarios.description: Chain's GEN deleteOn has been reached, but capacityImmutableUntil is in the future. Chain must not be deleted until lock clears.

scenarios.name: Archive immutability blocks chain deletion
scenarios.description: GFS point in Archive is within archiveImmutableUntil. Chain deletion must wait for Archive lock to clear even after deleteOn and Capacity immutability have both passed.

scenarios.name: GEN window aligns to generationPeriodDays boundaries
scenarios.description: Points created in days 1-10 must belong to GEN-0 and points created in days 11-20 to GEN-1 when generationPeriodDays=10. deleteOn for each GEN must equal windowEnd + slaDays.

scenarios.name: GEN deleteOn extended when GFS point falls in window
scenarios.description: When a GFS weekly point belongs to a GEN, the GEN's deleteOn must be recalculated to max(default deleteOn, gfsDate + gfsWeeks*7). Standard non-GFS GENs must keep original deleteOn.

scenarios.name: GEN lifecycle state is monotonic: Pending → WaitImmutability → Deletable
scenarios.description: A GEN must never go backwards through lifecycle states. Once Deletable it must not revert to Pending or WaitImmutability on a later day.

scenarios.name: All three tier immutability locks interact correctly
scenarios.description: With non-zero immutability on all three tiers, deletion must wait until ALL locks expire, even if only one tier contains data at deletion time.

scenarios.name: GFS W+M+Y × Move × Archive: cardinality and tier residency
scenarios.description: Mixed GFS with move mode and archive. Verify: weekly/monthly/yearly counts, tier residency per point, incremental-free Capacity after each chain archives, no premature archive entry.

scenarios.name: GFS W+M+Y × Copy × Archive: residue and gate
scenarios.description: Mixed GFS with copy mode and archive. Non-GFS Capacity residue must clear immediately after GFS point archives. Archive gate is point-age-based.

scenarios.name: GFS W+M+Y × Copy × Archive × Immutability (all 3 tiers): 3-way interaction
scenarios.description: High-risk 3-way: mixed GFS stacking, copy mode, archive, and all-tier immutability. Verify correct interlock between archive gating, capacity residue clearing, and GEN immutability locks.

scenarios.name: GFS Monthly × Move × Perf Immutability: GEN deleteOn vs immutability interlock
scenarios.description: Monthly GFS extends GEN deleteOn. Combined with Perf immutability this requires both deleteOn and lock to clear before prune/delete. Neither alone should be sufficient.

scenarios.name: Short retention × long GFS yearly: chain outlives retention by years
scenarios.description: With retention=7 and yearly=5 (5 years), chains sealed early must survive for 5 years because of GFS tag. Verifies GFS protection overrides count+SLA expiry for the full GFS window.

scenarios.name: Large generationPeriodDays with GFS and immutability
scenarios.description: generationPeriodDays=30: each GEN covers a full month. Verifies GEN window aligns correctly at 30-day boundaries and deleteOn is computed properly with monthly GFS extension.

scenarios.name: Copy+Move mode with GFS W+M and archive
scenarios.description: copyEnabled+moveEnabled simultaneously. Verifies both copy semantics (Capacity stamped at creation) and move semantics (Performance removed after offloadAfterDays) apply correctly, with correct archive gating.

scenarios.name: SOBR Move no-GFS: archive tier should remain empty
scenarios.description: With hasArchiveTier=true but no GFS policy, only GFS-tagged points may enter Archive. Archive tier must remain empty throughout the entire run.

scenarios.name: Retention variant retention=7 with W+M GFS
scenarios.description: Retention=7 paired with GFS to stress-test boundary interaction at the shortest practical retention. Chain should seal every 7 days and GFS must survive past that.

scenarios.name: Retention variant retention=60 with W+M+Y GFS
scenarios.description: Retention=60 with full GFS stack. Many chains coexist; verifies base identity remains oldest across all, GFS caps are respected across many active+inactive chains simultaneously.

scenarios.name: High change-rate adversarial: 40% daily delta over 2 years
scenarios.description: Stress scenario with extreme daily churn (40%) to catch storage or pruning behavior that appears stable at 5% but fails under heavy write amplification.

scenarios.name: Short retention adversarial: retention=3 over 3 years
scenarios.description: Very short retention with GFS enabled to stress frequent chain sealing/deletion. Ensures cleanup remains stable and restore points do not accumulate over long duration.

scenarios.name: Mid-run policy change: retention 7 → 30 on day 180
scenarios.description: Retention is expanded from 7 to 30 restore points partway through a 365-day run. Validates that the engine correctly grows the active chain toward the new limit, that old chains are not orphaned, and that GFS cardinality stays within limits throughout the transition.

scenarios.name: GFS-only policy: weekly=52 with minimal daily retention
scenarios.description: Stress test where daily retention is set to 1 (near-zero daily RPs) while weekly GFS keeps 52 weeks. After 2 years the engine should hold exactly 52 weekly GFS snapshots and no more. Validates GFS dominance over retention-based pruning.

scenarios.name: Two jobs sharing one repository
scenarios.description: Two independent backup jobs (different retention and GFS policies) write to the same DAS repository. Validates that chains do not cross-contaminate between jobs, each job maintains its own global base, and storage accounts for both jobs. Checks that inactive chain drift stays bounded across both job lifecycles.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: weekly GFS cardinality exact on every Saturday
scenarios.description: Every Saturday the weekly GFS count must equal min(weeks elapsed since start, gfsPolicy.weekly). Validated by oracle that computes expected count from dates, not from engine state.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: monthly and yearly GFS cardinality across calendar
scenarios.description: Each last-Saturday-of-month count must equal min(months elapsed, gfsPolicy.monthly). Each last-Saturday-of-December count must equal min(years elapsed, gfsPolicy.yearly).

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: per-point tier residency vs expected schedule
scenarios.description: Oracle computes expected tier set for each point on each day based on creation date, offloadAfterDays, archiveAfterDays, chain status, and GFS flag. Diffs against actual hasPerformanceData/hasCapacityData/hasArchiveData.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: GEN lifecycle state per day matches expected dates
scenarios.description: Oracle computes expected GEN state (Pending/WaitImmutability/Deletable) based on deleteOn and immutableUntil dates. Diffs against getCurrentGenerations() output each day.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: chain phase transitions match expected schedule
scenarios.description: Oracle predicts chain phase per day: Active, Inactive, OffloadPending, OffloadComplete, PerfPruned, Deleted. Diffs against actual chain and restore-point state each day.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: SOBR copy-only full lifecycle trace
scenarios.description: Copy mode: every new point immediately gets Capacity copy. Oracle tracks Perf+Cap dual occupancy per point, then Archive entry timing for GFS points, then Capacity residue clearing.

scenarios.name: Oracle diff: DAS W4+M8+Y2 weekly-only GFS points have non-zero storage
scenarios.description: Regression guard for bug fix: weekly-only GFS SyntheticFull points in a W+M+Y policy must contribute their incremental footprint (fullSize * changeRate) to used storage, not zero. Also validates GFS cardinality matches calendar expectations. Matches the exact user-reported scenario: 2TB source, 5% change, 10% growth, 14d retention, W4+M8+Y2 DAS.
